settings.keepHint: Between 1 and 365 days. How often each fault happened is kept for a year whatever this says, so a chart never develops a hole where the events were removed.
settings.acceptHint: Turned off, the address keeps answering and nothing is stored - which is what stops a crash loop filling this project while somebody works on it.

client.hint: Set it as the DSN of any Sentry client. Events older than {days} days are removed; how often each fault happened is kept.
client.deleteBody: Every fault it recorded goes with it, and the address stops being accepted.

issues.noneHint: No fault in this project matches what you are looking at.
issues.howOften: How often over the last {days} days

issue.pruned: Every occurrence of this has been removed by the project's retention. How often it happened is kept.
issue.deleteBody: Every occurrence goes with it. If it happens again it comes back as a new fault.

page.title: Telemetry
page.description: What your applications report when they break, and what Polaris reports about itself. Open a project for its faults and the address to point a Sentry client at.

internal.label: This network, and anything listed
internal.hint: Where an application deployed by Polaris reports from. Reports arriving from the open internet are turned away.

listed.label: Only the addresses listed
listed.hint: For a reporter that lives somewhere known - one server, one build runner.

anywhere.label: Anywhere
anywhere.hint: What a browser client needs, because its reports come from the addresses of the people using it. The client rules and the key still apply.

reasons.address: the address is not one this project accepts
reasons.client: the client does not match the rules
reasons.secret: the key was missing or wrong

rules.refused: {count, plural, one {One report was turned away} other {# reports were turned away}}{hasIp, select, yes { - the last from {ip}} other {}}{hasAgent, select, yes { ({agent})} other {}}{hasReason, select, yes {, because {reason}} other {}}{hasTime, select, yes { <time></time>} other {}}
rules.onlyThese: Only these may report. Name at least one.
rules.onTop: Accepted on top of this network.
rules.keyHint: A second value the reporter has to send, as an <header></header> header or an ordinary bearer token. A Sentry client that lets you set transport headers can carry it; one that does not cannot, which is why this is off unless you turn it on.
rules.keyInUse: A key ending {tail} is in use. It is stored as a digest and cannot be shown again - turn this off and on to make another.
